hypothesis: Who the household is (demographics) and when the snapshot is (calendar) predict 4-week spend.
transformation_description: Baseline: demographic codes, has_demographics, snapshot day index, week-of-year.

hypothesis: A household's recent purchasing behaviour (spend and trip counts over trailing windows, recency, basket size, trend) predicts its next-4-week spend far better than demographics.
transformation_description: Replaced baseline with RFM features: spend/trips at 28/56/84/112/168/364d windows, days_since_last, avg basket, 28d trend, weekly rate, active weeks.
reasoning_summary: Future 4-week spend is strongly autocorrelated with recent spend frequency and recency; RFM is the standard predictor of near-term grocery spend.

hypothesis: Future 4-week spend follows the household's recent 28-day spend sequence: adding per-window spends (up to 14 windows incl. same window last year), trends, volatility, and long-run spend rate to E001's RFM improves validation MAE.
transformation_description: Added 13 aligned-window spend features (w1..w14, trips for w1..w6), trend ratios (w1/w2, (w1+w2)/(w3+w4)), mean/std/CV over w1..w6, spend_w13 ratio vs recent mean, spend_per_28d_all, tenure_28d.
reasoning_summary: Aligned 28d window spends capture recency-weighted level, trend and seasonality (incl. year-ago window) that the coarse RFM windows miss; correlations ~0.79-0.82 with target.

hypothesis: Future 4-week spend tracks the household's long-run baseline and trip cadence (mean basket size, inter-trip gap mean/CV, weekly spend level and variability, active-week ratio, tenure, exponentially-weighted spend) and mean-reversion toward the usual 4-week level, beyond what recent 28-day windows capture.
transformation_description: Added 23 features to E002's table: trip-gap stats (mean/std/max/CV), basket mean/std, weekly spend mean/std/median, active-week ratio, tenure, EW spend at 4 half-lives, spend_per_trip, plus usual_4w (mean of w2-w6) and ratio_recent_usual (w1/usual).
reasoning_summary: Recent-window spend is noisy; long-run level, regularity, and mean-reversion ratios should stabilize predictions of the next 4 weeks and improve on E002's MAE 61.354.

hypothesis: Beyond recent spend cadence, what a household buys (department/fresh/private-brand mix), how it shops (store loyalty, basket size/composition, day-of-week and time-of-day rhythm), its discount/coupon engagement, demographics, and campaign exposure all predict its 4-week future spend level.
transformation_description: Added 76 features to E003's table: department spend shares (16 depts x 84/364d), fresh share, private/national brand share, discount shares (coupon/retail), store count + top-store share, basket line/unit counts, evening share, mean trans_time, top-day-of-week share, department entropy/diversity, demographics (7 ordinal/categorical cols), campaign targeting counts, coupon redemption counts/recency.
reasoning_summary: Spend level is driven by basket composition and shopping style: households buying fresh food weekly or large baskets have recurring high spend, while discount- and coupon-heavy patterns signal promo-driven, lower-margin spend. Demographics and campaign targeting add a household-type prior for the third of households with data.

hypothesis: Retailer marketing exposure adds predictive signal beyond RFM/cadence: households recently targeted by campaigns, actively redeeming coupons, or concentrating spend on displayed/mailed items spend differently in the next 4 weeks; per-household promo-discount shares capture price sensitivity.
transformation_description: Added 21 marketing features to E003's table: campaign-target counts (total/84d/168d, by type, active-now, recency), coupon-redemption counts/recency/campaign diversity, 8-week and 4-week display/mailer spend shares and displayed-product counts, and 84d shares of coupon/loyalty/match discounts.
reasoning_summary: Marketing exposure (targets, coupons, displays) and promo sensitivity are unused signals that plausibly modulate near-term spend; E004 showed product-mix features hurt, so a compact marketing block is the better next direction.

hypothesis: Demographic segments (age, income level, household size, homeownership, kids) shift the spend baseline: adding one-hot demographics to the E003 RFM/cadence table improves prediction for the third of households with demographics, and the has_demo indicator lets the model adjust for the rest.
transformation_description: Added 43 one-hot demographic dummies plus has_demo indicator to E003's 66-feature table (total 110 features).
reasoning_summary: Demographics correlate with spend capacity and trip frequency; the only proxy candidate that improved holdout MAE (63.16 vs 63.34), so it should add modest signal on top of saturated RFM features.

hypothesis: Future 4-week spend is best captured by a recency-weighted spend level (EWMA over multiple half-lives) plus the shape of the household's 28-day block spend history (level, variability, trend, activity regularity, year-ago block) and global week-of-year seasonality, on top of the E003 RFM/cadence core and demographic dummies.
transformation_description: Added 32 features to E006's table: EWMA spend/trips (half-lives 14/28/56/112d), fine 7/14d windows, 13 aligned 28-day block stats (mean/median/std/cv/active-fraction/slope/zero-run/year-ago), days_since_last, store breadth, active days, and mod-52 week-of-year sin/cos.
reasoning_summary: EWMA and block-shape features summarise the spend trajectory more smoothly than raw window sums, and the year-ago block plus mod-52 seasonality capture periodic shopping patterns that the snapshot-day index in E000 could not generalise to validation days.

hypothesis: Household spend is seasonal: spend in the same 28-day calendar window one year earlier (and its neighbours) predicts the next 4 weeks, beyond recent-window RFM and demographics.
transformation_description: Added 14 seasonal features to E006's 110-feature table: year-ago aligned 28d window spend/trips/coverage, adjacent windows l336/l392, year-ago basket size, ratio of year-ago spend to recent 28d and to 364d baseline.
reasoning_summary: Year-ago aligned-window spend correlates ~0.45 with the target on covered train rows and is available for ~90-100% of validation rows, so it adds a largely independent signal to the RFM+demographics model.

hypothesis: The signal in marketing exposure, purchase composition (dept/brand/store mix), and fine EWMA trailing windows is additive: combining the E008 table with all three blocks in one model lowers validation MAE below E008's 60.732.
transformation_description: Union of E008's 120-feature season+demo table with marketing (21), composition (60), and fine-EWMA (30) blocks, prefixed m_/c_/e_, 230 features total.
reasoning_summary: E005/E004/E007 showed each block adds ~0.3-0.5 MAE alone; a single model over all blocks may capture complementary interactions the separate models missed.

hypothesis: Beyond recent spend levels, future 4-week spend is predicted by activity continuity and spending stability: max purchase gap, active-week/window coverage, volatility (CV, std) of the aligned 28-day spend sequence, trend slope, trip concentration, tenure/lifetime scale, and basket-scale metrics (units, lines, distinct products per trip).
transformation_description: Added 18 behaviour-continuity/volatility features (b_*) to E008's 120-feature season+demo table (total 140).
reasoning_summary: Households that churn (large gaps, low coverage) or have unstable spend sequences should have different future spend than their recent level alone implies; lifetime scale and basket size add level information orthogonal to the 28d windows already present.

hypothesis: Future 4-week spend is systematically shifted from a household's trailing 28-day spend by a household-specific carry-over factor: historical (trailing-28d → following-28d) spend pairs, recency-weighted, calibrate the prediction beyond raw recent-spend levels.
transformation_description: Added 24 self-calibration features (sc_*) to E010's 140-feature table: per-household historical following-28d spend stats (mean/median/std/EWMA half-life 2&4 windows, active-only, year-ago), trailing→following ratios and carry-over factors, zero-window fraction, and t–f correlation.
reasoning_summary: E010's top predictors are trailing spend levels (r≈0.83); if a household's next window deviates from its trailing window in a stable, household-specific way, these lag-structure features should correct that bias and cut MAE.

hypothesis: Where and how a household shops shifts its future 4-week spend level beyond recency/cadence: primary-store identity and concentration, median unit price (spend per unit, 84d/364d), median package size, product breadth, and trip count over 364d.
transformation_description: Added 20 features to E011's 161-feature table: top-store one-hots (12 stores + other), store concentration share, median unit price 84d/364d, median package size 364d, distinct products 364d, distinct baskets 364d (all strictly causal, windows clipped to <= snapshot day).
reasoning_summary: Untried block: store identity, unit price, pack size and product breadth capture household price tier and basket repertoire, which plausibly shift spend level; proxy GBM showed the largest gain of all tested blocks.

hypothesis: The mapping from recent spend to future 4-week spend is multiplicative and demographic-segment-heterogeneous: log-transformed spend/EWMA/self-calibration levels plus spend×demographic interaction terms capture non-additive structure that E011's raw-scale features miss.
transformation_description: Added 50 features to E011's 161-feature table (total 211): log1p transforms of 12 spend/trip/EWMA/self-calibration features, plus 30 spend_28d × demographic-dummy interactions (age group, household size, homeowner, kids).
reasoning_summary: Log transforms linearise a multiplicative spend process and interactions let the model learn segment-specific spend→future-spend slopes; demographic one-hots gave the largest single gain so far (E006), so segment-specific slopes are a natural next step.

hypothesis: Where and how a household shops shifts its future 4-week spend beyond recency/cadence/self-calibration: top-store one-hots, store concentration, average unit price, product variety, and shopping timing (hour-of-day, day-of-week concentration) add signal.
transformation_description: Added 27 features to E011's 161-feature table (total 188): the previously untested store/price/variety block (top-12 store one-hots, store_share, unit_price_84/364, package-size median, nprod_364, nbask_364) plus new shopping-timing features (mean hour, hour std, morning/evening spend shares, day-of-week HHI and breadth, n_stores, top-store share).

reasoning_summary: Store loyalty, price tier, and variety reflect household size and stock-up behaviour that cadence features miss; timing patterns proxy work schedules that shift trip frequency. This is the first valid test of the store/price block since E012's table accidentally dropped the parent features.

hypothesis: Where and how a household shops shifts its future 4-week spend beyond recency/cadence/self-calibration: store concentration, unit price level, product variety, package size, and shopping timing (hour-of-day, day-of-week, store count) add signal.
transformation_description: Added 27 features to E011's 161-feature table (total 188): the previously untested store/price/variety block (retry of E014 with a valid table path).
reasoning_summary: Store loyalty, price tier and shopping habits plausibly mark heavy vs light shoppers; E012's failure may have been due to redundant one-hots, so this adds a leaner block with concentration/price/variety/timing instead.

hypothesis: Households with similar recent purchase trajectories (weekly spend pattern, 4-week level, recency) have similar following-4-week spend, so a k-nearest-neighbour forecast over other households' past aligned windows — a 'twin' forecast built only from data observable at the snapshot — adds predictive signal beyond the household's own trailing windows and self-calibration features.
transformation_description: Added 4 twin/kNN features to E011's 161-feature table: tw_k30 (inverse-distance weighted mean following-28d spend of 30 nearest reference rows pooled from t-28 and t-56 aligned windows, excluding the household's own rows), tw_k10 (k=10 variant), tw_ratio (w1 * neighbourhood mean of future/last-28d ratio, clipped to [0,4]), tw_diff (tw_k30 minus w1).
reasoning_summary: The twin forecast is structurally different from all existing features: it pools outcomes across households rather than summarising one household's own history. Local checks show it is well calibrated in the zero-spend regime (predicts 23.9 vs actual 24.8 on trailing-28d==0 rows) and its residual signal correlates only 0.42 with the household's own trailing-window residual, so it may help where self-calibration saturates.

hypothesis: Price-sensitivity behaviour (deal/coupon reliance), trip-gap hazard (whether the household is overdue relative to its own inter-trip cadence), and in-store display/mailer exposure each carry incremental signal about future 4-week spend beyond E011's recency/cadence/self-calibration features.
transformation_description: Added 36 features to E011's 161-feature table (total 197): deal/coupon shares, deep-deal share, redemption counts at 84/364d (13); trip-gap distribution stats, days-since-last vs median-gap hazard, zero-purchase stretch, short-window trips (14); display/mailer spend shares and line fractions (9).

reasoning_summary: Deal-seeking and gap-hazard capture whether a household is about to lapse or is discount-driven (lower future spend), while promo exposure plausibly shifts near-term baskets; offline inner-CV screening showed the union reducing proxy MAE vs E011.

hypothesis: Fine-grained recent activity (7/14-day spend and trips), a shorter-half-life EWMA level, forward-window means (F56/F84), recent-ratio volatility, zero-streak/active-fraction, and persistence products (recent 28d spend × forward-ratio/carryover stats) sharpen the recent-to-future mapping beyond E011's coarser features.
transformation_description: Added 20 x_* features to E011's 161-feature table (total 181): 7/14d spend+trips, EWMA level hl=2, forward EWMA hl6/hl8, F56/F84 means, ratio std/EWMA, zero streak, active frac 13, and 7 persistence products (recent spend × forward-ratio/carry/level stats).
reasoning_summary: E011's self-calibration uses coarse 28d windows; finer recent activity and direct recent×forward persistence terms may capture imminent churn/acceleration that coarse windows miss, and the harness model may exploit interactions my local ridge proxy could not.

hypothesis: Churn-hazard features (trip-gap distribution, hazard, near-term trip counts, activity fraction) plus a second-generation self-calibration block (shrunken T→F regression on aligned 28-day pairs, EWMA ratio, zero-T carryover) add predictive signal on top of E011's recency/cadence/season/demo/self-calibration features.
transformation_description: Added 33 features to E011's 161-feature table (total 194): 14 hazard_* trip-gap/hazard features + 18 c2_* shrunken-pair-regression self-calibration features (c2_pred, c2_pred6, c2_ratio_ew, c2_f_ew, c2_f_mean, c2_slope, etc.), leaving out the earlier deal/timing/display blocks that showed no gain.
reasoning_summary: Trip-gap hazard captures imminent-churn timing that pure spend aggregates miss, and the shrunken aligned-pair regression is a direct structural model of the 28d→4w mapping; both add orthogonal signal to E011's trailing-window features.
